mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of at least 0.5% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -0.5% and HOUST < -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in the federal funds rate below 3% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive monetary easing, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.75pp in one month AND UNRATE > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4% in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a flat or declining personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three months signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 0.4% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 <= 0% for same 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 persons for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly surge of at least 1% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a supply-side acceleration, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 1% AND HOUST > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered months at 5% significance.
